Hypothesis: Our revised hypothesis is that AHNAK2, when overexpressed in liver neoplasms, binds directly to geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes, leading to selective alterations in the geranylgeranylation of Rho/Ras GTPases. This modification disrupts their membrane targeting and consequent signaling, and by further altering RAB-mediated vesicular trafficking, it synergizes with parallel oncogenic mechanisms including those mediated by NAA40, NEK2, and circRNA-AHNAK pathways. Through this cascade—beginning with AHNAK2 upregulation and culminating in enhanced cellular motility, angiogenesis, and metastasis—AHNAK2 plays an essential and previously underappreciated role in liver cancer progression. We will employ CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, proximity-labeling mass spectrometry, live-cell imaging, and integrated proteogenomic profiling to interrogate each step of this causal chain and to establish its functional significance in tumor aggressiveness.
Abstract: We propose that in liver neoplasms, the overexpression of AHNAK2 is not merely a bystander marker but a key regulator of oncogenic progression. Our revised hypothesis posits that AHNAK2 directly interacts with geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes to selectively perturb the geranylgeranylation of critical signaling proteins, notably Rho and Ras GTPases. This mis-modification causes a disruption in these proteins’ membrane localization and signal transduction, which in turn alters vesicular trafficking through cooperative interactions with RAB family proteins. Integrated within an oncogenic network that also involves NAA40, NEK2, and circRNA-mediated regulation, these events collectively drive enhanced cellular motility, angiogenesis, and metastasis. We plan to rigorously test this mechanistic pathway using cutting-edge technologies including CRISPR/Cas9-based gene editing to modulate AHNAK2 expression, proximity-labeling mass spectrometry to map protein-protein interactions, live-cell imaging for real-time tracking of vesicular dynamics, and comprehensive proteogenomic profiling to quantify downstream signaling alterations. This integrated approach leverages contemporary technological capabilities to provide novel insights and potential therapeutic targets in aggressive liver cancer phenotypes.
CausalChain: AHNAK2 upregulation -> Direct interaction with geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes (+ integration with NAA40, NEK2, circRNA-AHNAK pathways) -> Altered protein geranylgeranylation of Rho/Ras GTPases -> Disrupted membrane localization and signal transduction -> Cooperative modulation of vesicular trafficking via RAB proteins -> Increased cell motility, angiogenesis, and metastasis -> Adverse liver neoplasm prognosis
